| City | Typical ZIP Code |

```

This returns the straight‑line (great‑circle) distance in miles. Keep in mind that road distances are usually ~10–15% longer due to turns, detours, and traffic patterns—so round up a bit when planning.

---

### 2️⃣ Rough Fuel Requirement Calculation  
Assuming you’re driving a standard passenger sedan (~25 mpg), here’s a simple way to eyeball whether your tank will last:

| Item | Value |
|------|-------|
| Distance (estimated above) | e.g., **350 mi** |
| Vehicle MPG | **≈ 25 mpg** |
| Tank Capacity | **12 gal** (typical) |

\[
\text{Required Fuel (gal)} \approx \frac{\text{Distance}}{\text{MPG}}

\[

\]

That means you would need roughly **14 gallons** to make the trip nonstop at 25 mph. Your tank holds only 12 gal, so you’d run short unless you refuel en route.

---

4. Compare that to the gallons currently in your tank + the maximum capacity.
